Priya: Hi folksI just adopted my nephew and want to add him to my coverage. The adoption finalized 40 days ago but we just received the court decree explaining why it was delayed. Is this a QLE? I know open enrollment is over.
Marco (People Ops): Welcome to the fam and congrats! Adoption is a qualifying life event. Typically you have 30 days, but courts and agency delays are common reasons carriers allow exceptions.
Priya: What paperwork will we need? The decree is in English but theres a delay stamp from the court clerk dated about 20 days after finalization because of processing backlog.
Diane (Benefits): We'll need the signed court decree, the adoption agency placement records, and any documentation showing the processing timeline. If there are legal guardianship docs or foster-to-adopt chain paperwork include that too.
Priya: Also, the kid doesn't have a SSN yet. We applied but system says pending. Will that block enrollment?
Marco (People Ops): No, use "SSN pending" on the portal and upload the SSA application receipt. Carriers accept temporary docs and will follow up once SSN is issued.
Priya: If we get an exception approved, can dental and vision start immediately or do they have separate waiting periods?
Diane (Benefits): Dental/vision sometimes have separate effective dates but in QLE situations carriers usually align them to the event date. We'll confirm with the carrier. For major dental procedures there's often a waiting period but routine coverage typically begins with enrollment effective date.
Priya: Ok. Anything else I should do to make the exception likely?
Marco (People Ops): Use clear filenames and a short cover note explaining the timeline. Example: "Perez_Samuel_adoption_decree_2026-03-10.pdf" and include the portal ticket in the email to benefits@redwood.com. Also mark the portal form as "Exception - Court processing delay".
BenefitsBot: Submission received: Ticket BEN-1794567890 created. Intake team will triage.
Diane (Benefits): Turnaround: we'll submit to carrier with an escalation note. Expect 7-14 business days. If carrier asks for additional legal verification we'll let you know.
Priya: Thanks y'all. Uploading docs now. Appreciate the quick help!
Marco (People Ops): Happy to help 1 we'll update thread when we hear back.
Priya: One more Q: if the carrier grants retro coverage, how are claims handled for care that occurred before the decree was recorded?
Diane (Benefits): If retroactive approval is granted, eligible claims usually can be submitted for reimbursement subject to plan rules and submission windows. We'll help you collect itemized invoices and submit as part of the retro claims package.
